population.note: FICTIONAL. Of about 274M adults, 27.7% current is about 75.9M, 40.0% ever-used is about 109.6M, 12.3% used and off now is about 33.7M, and about 164M have never used. Ever-use rose 4.5 points, inside the 5.7 limit, and current use rose 2.7. Cycling: about 14.5 points of current users are on a second or later course, and about 4.5 points of the off-now group restarted and stopped again, so (14.5+4.5)/40.0 = 47.5%. This fits roughly 35% one-year persistence (45–50% on gated and continuation plans) and 36–47% restart within a year. The rise was smaller than the money implied because new public enrolment kept colliding with exits. Exits came from the Lilly 12 mg restriction (Sep 2033), DEXA-driven pauses, and continuation-standard suspensions in the 38 states plus DC that use it. Age check: 18–29 at 14.5% × 52M = 7.5M; 30–49 at 30.5% × 91M = 27.8M; 50–64 at 42% × 62M = 26.0M; 65+ at 21% × 69M = 14.5M. Total ≈ 75.8M ≈ 27.7%. The 65+ rate rose only 4 points despite the Medicare default because about one in four 65+ ever-users is now off on a medical pause or has a bone contraindication. Income thirds of 30/28.5/24.5 average 27.7. The bottom third rose with seven more Medicaid adopters, but it is also the group most often suspended for missed kiosk weigh-ins. About 1.1M adults are on therapy primarily for alcohol use disorder after the Feb 2034 approval, mostly people already on the drug who were reclassified, plus about 0.4M new starts. Never-users skew under 30, rural, residents of non-adopting states, people with contraindications and refusers by conviction. In high-uptake suburbs the refusers are the ones expected to explain themselves. Pediatric: 1.3% of about 73M under-18s is about 950k. About 820k are adolescents 12+ (Medicaid EPSDT and commercial). About 130k are aged 6–11, roughly 40k of them started since the Jun 2034 Wegovy approval and the rest were already on specialist off-label use. Roughly two children in five now live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Public programmes are now the default payer for anyone 65+ and for low-income adults in adopting states. Medicare Part D obesity benefit: eligibility unchanged (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity). The negotiated rate fell from $199 to $179/month from Jan 2034 under the Oct 2033 HHS deal. The $50 copay and the counselling visit continue. Medicare pays 20.6% of fills, about 15.6M users (about 14.3M aged 65+ plus about 1.3M disabled under-65): about 6.3M diabetes and about 9.3M obesity. Obesity-benefit gross is 9.3M × $179 × 12 ≈ $20.0B. Beneficiaries pay 9.3M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.6B, so about $14.4B falls to the programme. All Medicare incretin fills: 15.6M × $179 × 12 ≈ $33.5B gross. Medicaid: 38 states plus DC now take the 90% match under the continuation standard. Medicaid pays 17.7% of fills, about 13.4M users × $179 × 12 ≈ $28.8B gross before supplemental rebates. Combined public share is 38.2% of fills, about 29.0M users. Medicare is the largest single purchaser. Medicaid EPSDT covers the new 6–11 pediatric indication in every state, adopting or not. In 2034 the Medicare Trustees for the first time attribute Part A and Medicare Advantage costs to incretin-associated fractures: about 15,500 excess hip fractures × about $45k first-year cost ≈ $0.7B a year, plus vertebral fractures and falls.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $4–25/month, plus generic oral semaglutide and liraglutide–semaglutide combinations. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, and Chinese API underlies most of the global gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. In the US the 2033 settlement entry date arrived, but FDA has given only tentative ANDA approvals (see note), so there is still no US generic.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. The Sep 2031 settlements allowed US generic semaglutide entry from Jan 2033, but no ANDA reached final approval. Two Hyderabad fill-finish sites received warning letters, and FDA asked synthetic-peptide filers for comparative immunogenicity data. The first final approval is guided for 2035. Brands used the reprieve to cut prices step by step rather than face a cliff. Novo's portal pen price went to $179 (Mar 2033), and the Oct 2033 HHS deal put Medicare and Medicaid at $179 from Jan 2034. Current portal prices: semaglutide pens $179, tirzepatide $229 (from $279), orals $129–169 (Foundayo starting dose $129), retatrutide $349 direct and $1,499 list, amycretin $399 direct. Wegovy list stays $1,349. PBM net is about $155–175 under outcomes contracts. Payer mix of about 75.9M users: commercial 36.9% (28.0M), Medicare 20.6% (15.6M), Medicaid 17.7% (13.4M), cash/direct 19.2% (14.6M, including about 4.4M 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscribers), imported/counterfeit 5.7% (4.3M). Total 75.9M = 100%. About 80% of covering employers gate coverage, and about a fifth of those have now copied the CMS bone-pause code. Some employers shifted over-65 workers onto Medicare. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg; pediatric 6–11 from Jun 2034)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose, restricted in older women since Sep 2033)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder, moderate to severe (semaglutide 2.4 mg, Feb 2034; ASAM and VA/DoD guideline endorsement 2033)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (Wegovy, Jun 2034, with growth-velocity and bone-age monitoring in label)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, about 4.4M subscribers), listed in standard employer lifestyle catalogues
AUD prescribing with tirzepatide and orals, outside the semaglutide label
smoking and vaping cessation (trial reading out 2035)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric use under 6 under specialist care (rare)
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. next_gen_launch is none, so no new class reached the US market. MariTide (Amgen, GLP-1 agonist/GIPR antagonist antibody) got a complete response letter in Jun 2033 asking for 104-week hip BMD data, with resubmission expected 2035. Survodutide (GLP-1/glucagon) got a complete response letter for obesity in Mar 2033 on lean-mass and heart-rate data, and Boehringer refocused it on a MASH filing. Bimagrumab plus semaglutide was filed Sep 2034, so a decision cannot come before late 2035, and it is the most watched filing in the field. The new indications are existing products in new labels. Semaglutide AUD was filed Jan 2033 on two phase 3 drinking-days trials plus the VA pragmatic study, and approved Feb 2034. Wegovy 6–11 was filed Apr 2033 on STEP Young and approved Jun 2034. The smoking-cessation trial with SHAPS endpoints is still running. US incretin market 2034 is about $148B: 71.6M paying users × about $172 average net × 12. Ex-US is about $25B and eroding. Revenue is roughly flat because volume up about 12% met a price down about 10%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Pediatric 6–11 trials show rates similar to adults, with vomiting more frequent in escalation.
Rising in absolute numbers with the larger 65+ population, partly offset by fewer 12 mg starts after Sep 2033.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. A small rise in alcohol-related pancreatitis among AUD users complicates attribution.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL litigation ongoing, with the first bellwether trial set for 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A population problem. The 2034 Medicare claims update estimates about 1.7M long-term 65+ users meet sarcopenia criteria, up from 1.3M. In untrained users over 50, lean mass is about 30–40% of weight lost.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained. Body-composition monitoring is in the retatrutide 12 mg and amycretin labels. Annual DEXA is required for long-term 65+ Part D users. MA 'prescribed lifting' benefits are now offered by most large MA plans.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Third wave year. About 7.4M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use: 7.4M × 0.6%/yr × 0.35 ≈ 15,500 excess hip fractures a year against about 300,000 US total, plus vertebral fractures in cycling postmenopausal women. The Lilly disclosure (Jun 2033) showed women ≥60 on 12 mg retatrutide lost a mean 4.1% of total hip BMD at 104 weeks versus 1.6% on placebo. DEXA waits have improved to 8–14 weeks with mobile capacity.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Sep 2033 label change: 12 mg retatrutide is not recommended for women ≥60 with T-score ≤−2.0 unless they are on an antiresorptive, and Medicare requires prior authorisation for 12 mg. CMS extended the bone-pause code from 90 to 180 days (Jun 2034). DOJ civil cases against Novo (settled 2033 for $410M without admission) and Lilly (opened 2033).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in AUD trial populations with high baseline psychiatric comorbidity.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About 12% of 12 mg retatrutide users cross the SHAPS threshold versus about 5% of comparators. The AUD trials recorded SHAPS and found a smaller but nominally significant shift at 2.4 mg semaglutide. About 4.4M low-dose subscribers are still unmeasured apart from vendor surveys.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The AUD label mentions 'decreased interest in pleasurable activities' in adverse reactions, the first such text in any incretin label. FTC consent orders on anxiety claims stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Millions of regain episodes a year from gating, continuation suspensions and pauses. The 12 mg restriction caused a visible wave of step-downs and regain among women over 60 in late 2033.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The 180-day Medicare bone pause softens it; most private plans still have no exemption. The Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver (Mar 2033); an en banc petition is pending.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency in high-loss older users. In AUD users, thiamine deficiency is a specific concern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; the AUD label advises thiamine assessment; no FDA action on the class.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~8 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The adolescent bone-accrual subset signal persists in a larger sample but is not conclusive. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Full adolescent data due 2034 were submitted in Nov 2034 and are under FDA review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre calls slightly up with about 4.3M import users. Indian generics bought online are now often authentic, so harms are mostly dosing errors and cold-chain failures rather than fakes.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and seizures continue. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled. No individual prosecutions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. Trustees now cost them alongside fractures.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening is mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Three independent DEXA cohorts replicate it: same weight, less lean mass, more visceral fat after repeated cycles, worst in people over 50.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The 2034 joint guidance recommends resistance training before any planned pause. CMS cites it in extending the bone pause.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg; arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled as a precaution; CVOT readout expected 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth velocity and bone accrual in children 6–11
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. STEP Young showed slightly lower height velocity in a minority of rapid responders over 68 weeks, of uncertain significance. There are no long-term data, and about 130k children aged 6–11 are now exposed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The label requires growth monitoring and bone age at baseline and yearly. A 10-year registry is a postmarketing requirement.

food_and_beverage.state: Salty snacks are down about 3–4% a year and confectionery about 4–5%. Kids' snack lines feel the pediatric approval: lunchbox brands are reformulating toward 'growth protein' claims to fit the growth-monitoring language now used in pediatric visits. Bone-forward fortified dairy leads category growth. A third packaged-food group sold its candy portfolio to private equity in 2033.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of spirits volume decline, now about 3–4% a year. Beer is down too. The AUD approval moved heavy-drinker treatment into primary care, and distributors report the steepest losses among high-frequency buyers, the 10% of drinkers who buy most of the volume. Non-alcoholic and premium 'one good drink' formats are still the only growth. Bars in Nashville and Austin lean on events rather than rounds.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover in high-uptake suburbs is about 10–12% below 2028. Gram-priced bowls, half portions and on-plan kids' menus are standard. Weekend 'full table' nights and the no-gram rooms in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston keep traffic up at the margins. Bar-dependent casual dining lost most from the AUD indication.

apparel.state: Size churn in both directions continues. A one-time size-down wave in children's wear followed the 6–11 approval, and the late-2033 regain wave among older women came after the 12 mg restriction. Resale and rental sized for cycling keep growing.

fitness.state: Growing. Most large MA plans offer prescribed lifting. DEXA-plus-coaching chains are now in hundreds of strip malls, and mobile DEXA capacity cut waits. Staff qualified to coach older lifters remain the bottleneck, and community colleges in Ohio and Arizona launched certificates in 2034.

insurance.state: Employer coverage dipped to 64% as some firms pushed over-65 workers onto Medicare and others gated harder. About 80% of coverage is gated. Pharmacy trend is about +3% (volume up, price down). Medicare Trustees now count fracture costs. Life insurers ask untreated applicants with BMI ≥30 to explain, and two carriers added a question on DEXA history.

pharma.state: Volume grew about 12% at prices about 10% lower, so US revenue is flat at about $148B. Lilly's scandal cost it about 18% of market value and some 12 mg share, but tirzepatide and Foundayo held. Novo gained a two-year reprieve from the generic slip, plus the AUD and 6–11 labels. Indian generic makers hold tentative US approvals and wait. Bone-agent makers are winners again.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Normalised further. Among insured adults over 40, being on the drug is the default, and being off needs a short reason: 'bone pause', 'my DEXA', 'suspended', 'by conviction'. Older women who stepped down from 12 mg after the 2033 disclosure are a recognised cohort, rounder in the face and more watchful about stairs. Trained shoulders still signal a well-run regimen.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use is close across incomes (bottom 24.5% vs top 30%), but care quality is not. Top-third users get scheduled DEXA, antiresorptives and coaching. Bottom-third users get kiosk weigh-ins, continuation suspensions after missed verifications, and in non-adopting states, imported pens. Pediatric uptake in 6–11s is highest through Medicaid EPSDT in Tulsa, Memphis and the Rio Grande Valley, where pediatric obesity rates are highest. Some parents there call it relief, and some call it pressure from the school nurse.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals are the norm. Hosts plan for 'on' guests by default. Children's birthday parties now routinely split into a cake table and an 'on-plan' table, which is a new etiquette problem. Church potlucks and Sunday full tables persist as deliberate heritage.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list on/off/pausing, and some now list 'sober (sema)'. 'Unmedicated' remains a niche filter. Advice columns field complaints about partners who refuse to start, and about partners whose drinking stopped and whose fun went with it.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Medicalised and assumed to be managed, and now craving for drink is managed the same way. The backlash coalition kept its absolute size and gained a cause in the pediatric approval: Tulsa–Dallas 'appetite is a gift' congregations and Atlanta body-sovereignty collectives jointly oppose school-nurse referrals. Its other target is still 'weigh-in welfare'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. About 12% of 12 mg retatrutide users cross the SHAPS threshold versus about 5% of comparators. After the Sep 2033 restriction, 12 mg users fell from about 2.5M to about 2.0M, and total top-dose triple/dual users are about 6M, implying on the order of 400k excess cases of clinically meaningful anhedonia if causal. The AUD trials gave the first randomised SHAPS data at 2.4 mg semaglutide and found a small shift, which the label now mentions. About 4.4M low-dose 'calm/focus/craving freedom' subscribers (inside the 14.6M cash/direct users) are unmeasured except by vendors.
interior_life.framing: Feature in retail, side effect in clinic, treatment on the AUD label. 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' ($129–169) now route subscribers who screen positive on AUDIT-C to covered on-label prescribing, so the line between wellness product and treatment is blurrier. Users still call the bad version 'the grey'. Prescribers say 'reward modulation'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: 'Focus' subscriptions are routine reimbursable lifestyle items at large white-collar employers. EAPs now refer drinking cases to on-label semaglutide, and some return-to-duty agreements in trucking and utilities require verified adherence. Sales, hospitality and creative workers still dose down before pitches and service peaks. Unions bargain over gated-plan data, and some contracts have copied the 180-day bone pause.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Critics' 'grey era' label is now applied to sobriety-memoir television as much as mid-tempo pop. 'Written unmedicated' remains a niche selling point in Nashville. High-stimulus leisure (spice, loud venues, extreme sports) keeps growing. Bar culture in college towns has thinned, and campus events have shifted to daytime.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose, subscription and now AUD prescriptions. Couples in which drinking had been the shared habit report a new kind of distance after one partner starts. Dose-holiday weekends and 'restart' anti-nausea packs remain common.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Lilly disclosure produced the first bipartisan incretin hearing, about data integrity and not about price. The administration campaigned on the $179 Medicare rate in the 2034 midterms. The continuation standard and school-nurse referrals for 6–11s are the live fights. Drug courts in Kentucky and Ohio adding semaglutide to their Vivitrol menus drew a civil-liberties challenge. 'Calm voter' effects remain speculation.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and now visibly burned. After the Lilly disclosure it requested subgroup BMD analyses from every sponsor, restricted 12 mg in older women, issued CRLs to MariTide and survodutide, and kept generic ANDAs tentative on manufacturing and immunogenicity grounds. It approved AUD and 6–11 labels for semaglutide with monitoring requirements. FTC continues consent orders on claims. Import enforcement is selective, and individuals are not prosecuted.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Public default for 65+ and low-income adults: Part D obesity benefit at $179 from Jan 2034 with a $50 copay. The 90% Medicaid match is taken by 38 states plus DC. EPSDT covers 6–11 nationally. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard's core terms are unchanged: ≥80% PDC, a verified weight every 6 months, ≥5% loss at 6 months or a clinician override, and annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users. The bone pause was extended to 180 days in Jun 2034. Missing two verifications suspends coverage for 6 months, and roughly 1.1M public-plan suspensions were logged in 2034. Indiana and Arkansas 12-month rules were upheld by the Seventh Circuit (Mar 2033), with en banc pending. Ohio and Georgia state-employee plans tie a premium credit of up to 20% to verified adherence. BMI-linked wellness surcharges continue. Drug courts in several states accept semaglutide adherence as a probation condition.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still steers drivers toward tirzepatide. Fleets add DEXA for drivers over 55 and verified-adherence return-to-duty terms for drivers with alcohol violations. The Air Force allows waivers for applicants stable for 12 months. The Army now accepts AUD-indication users stable for 12 months on a case-by-case basis.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the world. The FDA warning letters to two Hyderabad plants, which held up US generics, became an irritant in US–India trade talks. Section 232 tariffs remain. Lilly's 12 mg allocation ended in 2033, partly because the restriction cut demand.

events.event: The settlement date for generic semaglutide passes with no US launch: FDA keeps every ANDA tentative after warning letters at two Hyderabad fill-finish plants and a request for immunogenicity data. Novo cuts its portal pen price from $199 to $179 the same week.

A former Lilly biostatistician tells the Senate HELP committee that a 2030 analysis showing women over 60 on 12 mg retatrutide lost 4.1% of hip bone density, against 1.6% on placebo, was labelled exploratory and kept out of FDA briefing materials. Lilly says the analysis was not prespecified. DOJ opens an inquiry, and in September FDA restricts the 12 mg dose in older women with low bone density.

HHS and manufacturers agree a $179 Medicare and Medicaid rate from January 2034. Seven more states adopt the continuation standard, bringing the total to 38 plus DC, and Ohio's and Georgia's state-employee plans tie premium credits to verified adherence.

FDA approves semaglutide for moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder, the first incretin label to mention reduced interest in pleasure. Within months, drug courts in Kentucky and Ohio add it alongside Vivitrol as an accepted probation option with verified adherence.

Medicare Trustees attribute about 15,500 excess hip fractures a year, roughly $0.7 billion in first-year Part A and Advantage costs, to long-term incretin use. CMS extends its bone-pause code from 90 to 180 days.

FDA approves Wegovy for children aged 6 to 11 with obesity, requiring yearly growth and bone-age checks; Medicaid EPSDT coverage applies nationwide and the first school-nurse referral programs start in the fall term

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide is legally allowed but held up only by tentative ANDA approvals. When FDA clears the Hyderabad sites, perhaps in 2035, the $179 public rate and every outcomes contract built on it will reprice at once. That leaves the fiscal case for the continuation standard, which was built on per-user cost, open to challenge.

The Lilly disclosure made every sponsor's subgroup bone analyses suspect. FDA's demand for re-analysis lands just as 130k children aged 6–11 begin a drug whose growth data run 68 weeks, and the adolescent bone dossier is under review.

Medicare pays $179 a month for the drug and now also counts about $0.7B a year in fractures. The 180-day bone pause protects seniors, but most gated employer plans still drop a 58-year-old for following the same advice.

The AUD label puts 'decreased interest in pleasure' into an approved indication. Meanwhile about 4.4M people buy that same effect as 'focus' or 'craving freedom', and drug courts now verify adherence. Treatment, product and condition of liberty are becoming the same pill.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The 503B compounding exclusion and the 503A injunction both still stand; compounded semaglutide has not returned to the legal US market.

The CMS continuation standard's core terms are unchanged: ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered from pharmacy claims, a verified weight every six months, ≥5% loss at six months or a clinician override, and annual DEXA for long-term users 65+.

prose.headline: The Pen Went Public: Medicare pays $179, Lilly's bone data surfaces, and third-graders get Wegovy
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2034 a little more than one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, about seventy-six million people. That is less of a rise than the money would suggest. The government has become the main buyer, the price has come down, and two new labels have been added. Over the same two years millions of people came off, because of a bone scan, a missed weigh-in, or a restriction on Lilly's strongest dose. The number of current users went up slowly because a large number left while a larger number joined.

Generic semaglutide was due in 2033 and has not arrived. The settlement allowed it, but the FDA did not approve any filing. Two plants in Hyderabad received warning letters, and synthetic-peptide makers were asked for more immunogenicity data. Indian generics hold tentative approvals and are waiting. Novo did not wait for a price collapse. It cut its portal pen price to $179 that spring, and in the autumn HHS fixed the same $179 for Medicare and Medicaid from January. Tirzepatide fell to $229 and the starting oral to $129. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, and almost nobody pays it. Prices have come down through deals, and access still depends on having coverage.

Coverage increasingly comes from the government. Medicare pays for about one fill in five and Medicaid for about one in six. Thirty-eight states and Washington now take the ninety-percent match and the continuation standard that comes with it: pharmacy-claims adherence, a verified weight every six months, five percent loss by month six. About a million people on public plans were suspended in 2034 for missing verifications. Ohio and Georgia now offer state workers a premium credit for staying adherent. The Seventh Circuit upheld Indiana's harsher waiver.

The most important news of 2033 came from inside Lilly. A former company statistician told a Senate committee that a 2030 analysis had been labelled exploratory and kept out of FDA briefing materials. It showed older women on the 12-milligram triple agonist losing hip bone density at more than twice the placebo rate. Lilly said the analysis was never prespecified, which may be true. The FDA restricted the dose in older women with low bone density, Medicare added prior authorisation, and a wave of women in their sixties stepped down and regained weight. The agency also rejected MariTide and survodutide that year. No new kind of drug reached the market.

In June the Medicare Trustees did something no budget score had done before: they counted the fractures. They estimated about fifteen and a half thousand excess hip fractures a year, costing roughly seven hundred million dollars in first-year hospital and rehabilitation care. The same month CMS doubled its bone-pause allowance to 180 days. Most employer plans have not followed. DEXA waits are down to two or three months, mainly because mobile scanners now park beside strip-mall gyms.

Two new labels widened what the drug is for. In February semaglutide was approved for alcohol use disorder, and its label is the first in the class to mention reduced interest in pleasurable things. Spirits volumes are falling faster, bars in college towns are quieter, and drug courts in Kentucky and Ohio now accept verified adherence alongside Vivitrol. In June Wegovy was approved for children aged six to eleven. Birthday parties in Tulsa now have two tables, one for cake and one for children on the drug.

The 'focus' subscriptions keep selling, about four and a half million of them, and they now send users who screen positive for drinking to a covered prescription. Being on the drug is ordinary. People who are off are asked to explain why, and the usual answers are a bone pause, a suspension, or a refusal on principle.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Krystal Moody has her coat on at 6:40 and Eli's lunch packed with the string cheese the clinic handout likes. At the Walgreens on 11th the kiosk is beside the blood-pressure cuff. She scans her Medicaid card, steps on, and waits for the green check. Last March she missed one, and she knows how much a second miss would cost her.

She drops Eli at Kendall-Whittier. He is nine, four months on the pen, and he no longer asks for seconds. The school nurse waves as they pass.

She spends the day on home visits. Mrs. Teague, eighty-one, is on a bone pause and frightened of the stairs. Krystal walks her to the mailbox and back. Mr. Ortiz keeps his Quiet subscription on the counter beside his sobriety chip and says the two are the same thing these days.

At 3:30 Eli's growth check is at the Medicaid clinic. He grew a little less than the chart line. Dr. Patel says it's within range and they'll look again in spring, and she writes the bone-age order. Krystal asks if she should stop his pen. Dr. Patel says no, not yet.

At Aaliyah's birthday that evening there are two tables. Eli goes to the one with cut fruit and doesn't look at the cake. Her sister Tasha, who has never started and says she never will, slides him a corner piece on a napkin. Krystal sees it and says nothing.

At home she takes her pill and sets the scale app reminder for April.
